rows.why: Item 8 asks what happens when a newly drawn code matches an existing one. The scenario says such a code is drawn again, and the pick redraws (giving up only after 1000 tries), so they agree. No item asks about the 14-day expiry or the unused starting state.
Nothing on the list asks whether redeeming grants access to that task only, or whether the code records who used it and when.
Item 7 asks how typed input is matched for case, spaces and dashes. The pick removes whitespace and '-' and uppercases before lookup, so lowercase, spaced or dashed input finds the same code.
Item 1 asks whether a code still works at the exact 14-day instant. The pick counts a code as expired once now >= expiresAt, so it works at 08:59:59.999 and fails as 'expired' at 09:00:00.

Item 3 is about redeeming a different code for a task the person can already reach. Item 4 is about which reason wins when several apply. Neither asks whether the person who used a code can redeem it again and succeed with nothing changing, and that is the open question here.

Item 5 asks whether codes can be revoked and what happens when you revoke a used, unknown or already-revoked code. The pick adds revocation and throws for used codes, which matches 'a used code cannot be revoked'.
Item 3 asks about redeeming a code for a task the person can already reach. The pick fails with reason 'already has access' and leaves the code unused, which is exactly what the scenario expects.
Item 12 asks how simultaneous operations are handled. The pick runs every operation one at a time through a promise queue, so of two simultaneous redemptions one succeeds and the other sees 'used'.
Item 2 asks what state a code used before expiry shows once its expiry time passes. The pick keeps it 'used' because the used check comes before the expiry check, which matches the scenario.
